# Sub-Agent Persistence Pattern

Audit sub-agents (`citation-audit`, `consistency-review`) write their
reports through the `put_data.py` wrapper — never the Write tool. One
mechanism for every persistence path keeps the session's allowlist
surface tiny.

## Invocation

The caller (the coordinator) gives the agent a SLUG. The agent runs
the wrapper with that SLUG and an output filename relative to the
slug directory.

Linux/macOS:

```
~/.claude/skills/cited-research/.venv/bin/python \
    ~/.claude/skills/cited-research/scripts/put_data.py \
    [SLUG] audit/<output-filename> <<'EOF'
[full report markdown]
EOF
```

Windows (git-bash):

```
~/.claude/skills/cited-research/.venv/Scripts/python.exe \
    ~/.claude/skills/cited-research/scripts/put_data.py \
    [SLUG] audit/<output-filename> <<'EOF'
[full report markdown]
EOF
```

Substitute `<output-filename>` for the agent's specific report name
(e.g., `citation-audit.md`, `consistency-review.md`).

## What happens next

The wrapper writes to `./.tmp-cited-research/[SLUG]/audit/<output-filename>`.
The coordinator promotes the file to the final deliverable location
(`<deliverable-dir>/audit/<output-filename>`) after the verification
phase completes. Agents do not perform the promotion themselves; the
allowlist boundary keeps agents writing only inside the tmp tree.

## Return value

After persisting, return a one-line summary as the agent's final
response (e.g., `"Citation audit complete; 27 citations graded."`).
The coordinator reads this summary to decide next steps.
